situation_note: Series C $400M at $3.8B (Oct 28, 2026), 600+ employees, 400+ customers; scaling fast in CNAPP, runtime detection and AI security
angle: Buyers who don't already know Upwind never meet it: AI builds every cloud-security shortlist from third-party lists that leave Upwind out, even though it describes Upwind accurately and often picks it once a buyer names it.

lead_claims.figure: 0.9% (1 of 116 answers to questions that don't name Upwind)
0 of 8 methodology-backed best-of lists ChatGPT cited name Upwind
92.0% (126 of 137) answers about Upwind with no confirmed error

opener.text: Congrats on the new CMO role, and on arriving the same month as a $400M Series C at a $3.8B valuation, less than nine months after the Series B.

caveats: Two platforms only (ChatGPT, Gemini); Google AI Mode collection stalled and Bright Data was paused, so Gemini stands in.
Recipient email follows the first.last pattern and is unverified; the domain may be catch-all. Verify with Hunter before sending.
C-051 and C-103 are MEDIUM confidence (single run, no re-run).
rationale: Upwind is a scaling company with a new CMO and fresh Series C money, so the natural audience is marketing, and the result is a sharp, non-obvious story rather than a generic 'you're invisible': AI describes Upwind accurately and picks it in close to half of head-to-heads once named, but almost never brings it up unprompted, and none of the methodology-backed best-of lists ChatGPT cited for these questions includes it. That points the new CMO at concrete, fundable work (buyer-guide submissions, review volume, a few fact pages) right as the budget arrives. The opener ties the CMO's start to the round, both sourced; the email asks for nothing beyond whether to send the report.
